ov: Seabirds, usually grey and white, with strong bills and webbed feet. Gulls eat almost anything and mostly stay near coasts or inland, rarely far out at sea. They can drink salt water, getting rid of the salt through glands in the skull that drain out of the nostrils.
len: 29 cm (little gull) to 76 cm (great black-backed gull)
wt: 120 g (little gull) to 1.75 kg (great black-backed gull)
rg: Coasts and inland waters; few species venture far out to sea.
df: Almost anything: fish, invertebrates, earthworms, rodents, eggs, carrion, seeds, fruit and human refuse.
fx: A gull’s jaws can unhinge to swallow large prey.
Gulls have been seen landing on surfacing whales to peck off pieces of flesh.
